A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IT-Optimization framework and share identifiable methods and experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; internal inconsistencies in v3 do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and the appendices report original NMR restraint, crystallographic density, and protein-complex confidence optimization experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, ablations, structural-validity measurements, additional protein cases, and runtime and compute-budget results.

M1.justification: The embedding updates, nested optimization, experimental objectives, ProteinEBM reweighting, and regularizers are retained. Algorithms 2–3 are unchanged. Boltz-2 applies the existing procedure, while the new surrogate objective is introduced for theoretical analysis rather than as a replacement empirical algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds whole-protein density fitting without pre-modeled structures for 4NE4 and 5TEU, plus four larger NMR targets in Tables 19–20. These extend coverage within the existing modalities. The three X-ray targets omitted from some later tables still have cosine-similarity results in Table 11, so they are not entirely removed.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates ESMFlow, AFCluster, and BioEMU alongside the retained comparators for NMR and crystallographic benchmarks (Tables 5–6 and 14–16). AFCluster previously served as an MSA initialization tool, not an evaluated comparator. This substantially expands the comparison set; Boltz-2 is a tested backbone rather than a competing baseline.

E3.justification: V3 introduces matched 200/800-denoiser-call comparisons, controlled hyperparameter sweeps, NOE subsampling, Boltz-2 evaluations, and additional ESS, interface-quality, and geometry metrics. Relaxation is reported as AMBER99SB instead of AMBER99, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Table 9's default inverse temperature of 0.6 conflicts with the retained 1.68 setting in Section C.3.4.

E4.justification: New analyses examine hyperparameter sensitivity, annealing and energy smoothing, effective sample size, sparse-restraint geometric validity, MolProbity quality, and matched-compute performance (Tables 7–10, 17, and 20). Figures 10 and 14 add interface-accuracy diagnostics and transfer to Boltz-2. These substantially extend v1's convergence, seed-stability, and selected structural case studies.

E5.justification: V1 Table 8 already reports estimates with variability across five independent runs. V3 Figure 15 explicitly identifies the summaries as means and standard deviations, clarifying the uncertainty reporting. The run count remains five; the expanded target set does not establish an increase in repetitions or a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Core NMR Tables 3–4 are retained, but v3 adds extensive comparator, ablation, validity, runtime, and transfer results. Table 20 newly shows budget-dependent rankings: for 2B3W, Guidance/IT-Opt violation rates are 13.7%/14.4% at 200 calls and 13.7%/8.4% at 800 calls. R-factor and repeated-run entries for 4NPU, 3QDA, and 4RMW are removed, although their cosine scores remain.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines a trajectory-averaged surrogate and displacement oracle, analyzes omitted-score and nested-drift bias, and introduces smoothness assumptions and variance bounds. Theorem B.8 supplies an O(1/K) stationarity bound with a bias/variance floor, followed by an expected-ascent corollary and proofs. V1 contains no corresponding convergence analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central contributions and confidence-inflation warning. Section 2.1 explicitly extends the claimed independence to the underlying protein generator, and Section 2.2 adds a claim of physically plausible crystallographic ensembles. These are limited extensions of the existing contribution framing.

C2.justification: The new theory substantially qualifies optimization guarantees through biased surrogate gradients and conditional near-stationarity, rather than unconditional posterior ascent. V3 also adds interpretations concerning matched-compute advantages and sparse-restraint robustness. Section 5.3 newly describes ipSAE as largely unchanged, conflicting with the retained increases in Figure 13; this changes interpretation without reversing the plotted results.

D1.justification: Table 19 and Section C.2.1 add measured GPU memory and per-loop runtime information, and Table 17 identifies phenix.molprobity for structural validation. Relaxation documentation changes to AMBER99SB. Most hardware, software, preprocessing, optimizer, and hyperparameter details were already present in v1 and are retained after relocation.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of Richman et al.'s repulsive guidance and citations supporting biased-gradient analysis, BioEMU, DockQ, and MolProbity. Some background and benchmarking references are replaced. The principal positioning against coordinate-space guidance and MSA manipulation remains; publication updates to existing works do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. V3 makes localized language and terminology edits, adds acknowledgments and author-information changes, and moves implementation details earlier within the supplemental material. The substantial scientific additions do not amount to wholesale rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds benchmark-summary violin plots, interface-metric bar plots, and Boltz-2 convergence plots. It moves v1 Figure 8 into the main text as Figure 7 and replaces the seed-stability table with a broader plotted comparison. Appendix figures are regrouped, numerous tables are added, and table captions and layouts are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny through broader baselines, controlled ablations, structural-validity checks, and matched-compute comparisons that v1 lacked. Runtime reporting and conditional theoretical analysis also make the method easier to assess. The conflicting temperature settings and ipSAE interpretation remain material weaknesses, but the added evidence meaningfully addresses important gaps in v1's validation and supports a substantial net improvement.
